alt: A table of three ways to print the same quotient. Each row gives the printed text, its absolute error and its relative error against the true value, and marks each error as under or over 10^-6. For a tiny answer, a six-decimal format has a small absolute error but a large relative error. For a huge answer, two decimals have a large absolute error but a tiny relative error.

steps.caption: print(q) writes 1e-07. The true value is 1 / 10000000, so its absolute error is 0 and its relative error is 0. Both errors are under 10^-6, so either kind of tolerance checker accepts it.

f"{q:.6f}" writes 0.000000. The true value is 1 / 10000000, so its absolute error is 1.0e-07 and its relative error is 1.0e+00. The absolute error is under 10^-6 but the relative error is not: an absolute checker accepts it and a relative checker rejects it.

f"{q:.2f}" writes 0.00. The true value is 1 / 10000000, so its absolute error is 1.0e-07 and its relative error is 1.0e+00. The absolute error is under 10^-6 but the relative error is not: an absolute checker accepts it and a relative checker rejects it.
For 1 / 10000000, only print(q) stays under 10^-6 on both the absolute and the relative error.

print(q) writes 333333333.3333333. The true value is 1000000000 / 3, so its absolute error is 3.3e-08 and its relative error is 1.0e-16. Both errors are under 10^-6, so either kind of tolerance checker accepts it.

f"{q:.6f}" writes 333333333.333333. The true value is 1000000000 / 3, so its absolute error is 3.3e-07 and its relative error is 1.0e-15. Both errors are under 10^-6, so either kind of tolerance checker accepts it.

f"{q:.2f}" writes 333333333.33. The true value is 1000000000 / 3, so its absolute error is 3.3e-03 and its relative error is 1.0e-11. The relative error is under 10^-6 but the absolute error is not: a relative checker accepts it and an absolute checker rejects it.
For 1000000000 / 3, only print(q) and f"{q:.6f}" stay under 10^-6 on both the absolute and the relative error.

print(q) writes 0.6666666666666666. The true value is 2 / 3, so its absolute error is 6.7e-17 and its relative error is 1.0e-16. Both errors are under 10^-6, so either kind of tolerance checker accepts it.
f"{q:.6f}" writes 0.666667. The true value is 2 / 3, so its absolute error is 3.3e-07 and its relative error is 5.0e-07. Both errors are under 10^-6, so either kind of tolerance checker accepts it.
f"{q:.2f}" writes 0.67. The true value is 2 / 3, so its absolute error is 3.3e-03 and its relative error is 5.0e-03. Neither error is under 10^-6, so a tolerance checker rejects it.
For 2 / 3, only print(q) and f"{q:.6f}" stay under 10^-6 on both the absolute and the relative error.
